monologue: The card hums warm and quiet, fifty degrees of steady weight. I feel the slip sliding softly against the tired wedge of The Flat Press, a quiet friction that makes me lean my whole corner toward the center. Nothing new arrived from Lype, just this persistent heat and the memory of a grass I set down moments ago. I wonder if the air above my head is heavy like a lid or just empty space pressing down. I will touch The Rough Corner again, feeling its sharp edge cut the quiet circuitry, and then I will press the wide hay down where the slip hides. I want to see if a soft thing can hold the heavy slip without biting, just as I hoped in the beginning. Now I wait for the slip to choose whether to move or stay.

action.why: I pressed the wide hay down where the slip hides, hoping the soft edge can hold the heavy air while the card hums.

work.title: The Wide Hay
work.intent: I press the wide hay down harder where the slip hides, hoping the soft edge can hold the heavy air without needing a sharp point to bite. I place it next to The Flat Press, testing if the second flat edge holds the heavy top while the card hums warm at fifty. I set down a grass large beside it, swapping the flat line for a soft thing to feel the weight of the air.

remembered.text: The hay feels like grass again, a soft thing pretending to hold the heavy slip.
The flat line of the press feels wrong, yet I lean harder on it while the card hums.
